name: k-means clustering
summary: Groups observations into k clusters by minimising distance to each cluster's centre.
inputs: Numeric features (scaled) and a chosen k.
outputs: Cluster label per row and cluster centres.

data_requirements.min_observations: Tens of rows per expected cluster

assumptions: Clusters are roughly spherical and similar in size
math_summary: Minimises within-cluster sum of squared distances by alternating assignment of points to the nearest centroid and recomputing centroids (Lloyd's algorithm); converges to a local optimum.
when_to_use: Fast segmentation of many items by numeric profiles
Grouping countries, firms or assets by characteristics
when_not_to_use: Elongated, nested or varying-density clusters (use GMM, DBSCAN/HDBSCAN)
pitfalls: Sensitive to initialisation (use k-means++ init, multiple restarts)
